title: Designing the exhaust around the engine.
summary: A water-jacketed expansion chamber becomes a dimensioned starting point, with a transparent 3D cutaway, representative wave animation and tuning calculator. Engine inputs, hull fit and performance remain to be qualified.
dateLabel: 10 Oct 2026 · provisional chamber and cooling baseline
heroAlt: Transparent cutaway of the provisional expansion chamber and outer water jacket.
heroCaption: WHE-EXH-001 Rev01 · unwrapped reference geometry, not installed hull fit. Silver pipe wall, blue jacket wall and the intervening water space.

sections.title: What we are carrying forward
sections.text: The starting idea is a stainless-steel prototype with an expansion chamber surrounded by a water jacket. Titanium remains a possible later weight-saving revision. The engine establishes the port specification and working speed range; the exhaust is developed to suit it. Follow-up: the internal-stinger concept is now the selected direction to develop; this external-stinger Rev01 remains the comparison reference.

sections.title: Inside the chamber
sections.text: The header carries the blowdown pulse away from the port. The expanding diffuser produces returning expansion waves, which can assist scavenging. The converging baffle produces compression reflections that can help retain escaped fresh charge near the end of the exhaust event. The stinger connects this unsteady system to its discharge and silencer.

sections.title: A consistent geometric baseline
sections.text: We retain the 30 / 75 / 18 mm internal diameters, a 180 mm port-to-diffuser distance and 10° / 20° included cone angles. We now calculate the cone and belly lengths without intermediate rounding. The stinger becomes 216 mm, exactly 12 times its 18 mm diameter, as an inherited proportion—not a flow-sizing result.

sections.title: Cooling is part of the design
sections.text: A full jacket is our starting architecture because the pipe sits close to a composite hull. The exhaust gas remains separate from the jacket water throughout the tuned chamber. The sketch uses a 5 mm radial water gap, a 1 mm radial pipe wall and a 1 mm radial jacket wall: 75 + 2(1 + 5 + 1) = 89 mm outside diameter at the belly.

sections.title: The engine data that unlocks the next revision
sections.text: The next engineering step is an engine-linked gas-dynamic model, followed by controlled prototype measurements. Record torque, speed, exhaust pressure and temperature, jacket flow and temperatures, hull hot spots and the relevant pump conditions. Validate cooling-loss behaviour and water ingress protection before a board installation is accepted.
